critique: Applied branch-staleness-by-commits-ahead, previously HELD the same day and then approved by explicit decision. Deviated from the literal proposal on purpose and said so in the ledger row: run 5 asked to replace tip-date staleness WITH commits-ahead, but commits-ahead measures divergence, not time - a branch 3 ahead and untouched 60 days would have scored identically to one created this morning. The real defect was narrower: git rebase preserves the author date and writes a new committer date, and the protocol never specified which one it read. So staleness now pins to the tip AUTHOR date, and ahead_by is recorded as a SEPARATE signal (0-ahead + stale = dead weight to delete; 12-ahead + stale = unmerged work at risk). Adding ahead_by threatened to reintroduce the per-branch API call whose removal took five proposals over three weeks, so the branch_tips cache was extended rather than bypassed: author_date refetches only on a branch SHA change, ahead_by also on a DEFAULT-branch SHA change since it is relative to a moving base, and pre-today cache entries with a bare date field are treated as a miss because there is no way to know which date they held. critique: Run 17. Fleet went from the quietest state on record to a small uptick: 1 open PR (new, TokenMonitorV2#1) where there were 0, issue count unchanged at 1 (Aether-OS#22, open on purpose). The PR resolves a Watch List item that had persisted since run 15 ("no PR backing reskin-phases-3-4") - local work had already moved on to a new reskin-phase-5 branch (19 and 20 ahead of main respectively, both pushed, so not at loss risk despite the size). Verified branch-tips cache diff caught exactly 3 changed/new branches out of 26 (agent-improvement/master via the sibling agent-learn loop's own commit, plus TokenMonitorV2's two reskin branches) and reused the other 23 - the cache is earning its keep. Two things this run adds to the record. First, false_positives is 1 (loop-derived), and it should not have taken this long to catch: the Aether-OS "1 commit on no remote branch" recommendation has been byte-identical since at least run 14 with zero human action, crossing the refinement-1 bar a run or more ago without anyone (loop or human) marking it - moved to Recent Noise now with an explicit decision ask (push, delete, or add to Human Decisions). Second, and this run's adjustment: refinement 5's stale-WIP check compares only the dirty-line COUNT run over run, and today it fooled itself - Aether-OS-livetest read as "unchanged for the 4th run" at 4 dirty lines, but the actual file set changed (e2e/livetest2.spec.ts is new, replacing nothing; the count coincidentally held).
